entities.summary: Pierius was a Christian priest who flourished as the probable head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria, conjointly with Achillas, during the reign of Theonas as bishop of Alexandria. He died at Rome after 309 and was commemorated by the Roman Martyrology on 4 November. This event is significant because it highlights the importance of Christian education and the rise of the Catechetical School as a major center of learning in the Mediterranean world. The school's influence extended beyond Egypt, shaping the intellectual and theological landscape of the Roman Empire. Pierius' legacy also underscores the complexities of religious and cultural exchange during the Late Antique period. The exact date of his death remains unknown, but his significance as a Christian leader and educator continues to be felt in the history of Christianity and the Mediterranean world.
